In order to satisfy this criterion, the petitioner must establish not only that the beneficiary has made
original contributions but that they have been of major significance in the field. For example, it may
support the record with evidence that a beneficiary's contributions have been widely implemented,
have remarkably impacted or influenced the field, or have otherwise risen to a level of major
significance in the field. Demonstrating ability as a skilled digital entrepreneur is not itself a
contribution of major significance; rather, the Petitioner must demonstrate that the Beneficiary has
impacted the field as a whole. Cf Visinscaia v. Beers, 4 F. Supp. 3d 126, 134-135 (D.D.e. 2013)
(upholding a finding that a ballroom dancer had not met a similar criterion in the regulations pertaining
to immigrants of extraordinary ability because she did not demonstrate her impact in the field as a whole).
The record does not include documentary evidence showing the widespread implementation of the
Beneficiary's work, that it has been seminal, or that it otherwise equates to an original contribution of
major significance in the field. users may, in its discretion, use as advisory opinions statements

collaborated and consulted. However, those letters do not establish that he has made original business
related contributions of major significance in his field.

Evidence that the alien has been employed in a critical or essential capacity for
organizations and establishments that have a distinguished reputation. 8 C.F.R.
§ 214.2(o)(3)(iii)(B)(7).
On appeal, the Petitioner maintains that it has employed the Beneficiary in a critical or essential capacity.
The Director determined that although the record shows that the Beneficiary has been employed in a
critical or essential capacity for the petitioning company as its CEO and co-founder, the Petitioner did
not establish that it is or was a company with a distinguished reputation, as required by this criterion.
We agree with the Director's determination.
I I
The Petitioner provided two letters from a professor at ~ and the Petitioner's
president. He confirms that the Beneficiary has been CEO of the Petitioner since its inception in 2016,
and that the Beneficiary owns 25% of the company. He asserts that as a direct result of the
Beneficiary's "outstanding abilities" the Petitioner has grown "from zero to a projected annual income
I I
of over $500,000 in 2018." a professor atD and the Petitioner's COO, states
that the Beneficiary grew the Petitioner's "sales pipeline from $9,000 per year to over $360,000 per
year within a time frame from May 2017 to May 2018." On appeal, the Petitioner provides a 2018
profit and loss statement indicating the company has gross income in excess of $470,000.
While the aforementioned documentation indicates the current stage of development of the petitioning
company, it does not establish that it has a distinguished reputation in the field. Based on the foregoing,
the Petitioner has not established the Beneficiary's eligibility under this criterion.

Evidence that the alien has either commanded a high salary or will command a high
salary or other remuneration for services, evidenced by contracts or other reliable
evidence. 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(o)(3)(iii)(B)(8).
The record contains a paystub confirming that in 2018 Petitioner paid the Beneficiary a salary of $19,231.
Assuming that the Beneficiary will be paid a salary of $70,000 per year and other compensation in the
form of"equity in the company," as stated on the Form 1-129, we agree with the Director's conclusion
that the Petitioner has not established the Beneficiary's past or future salary is high in relation to others
in the field.
Within the Petitioner's response to the Director's request for evidence, the Petitioner submitted, as a
point of comparison, an O*Net printout from the Department of Labor, Office of Foreign Labor
Certification, reflecting that the Level 4 prevailing wage for market research analysts and marketing
specialists in the Beneficiary's geographic area is $80,766 per year. The Beneficiary's salary does not
exceed the Level 4 prevailing wage for the Petitioner's area.
5
Additionally, the prevailing wage only reflects the average wage paid to all similarly employed workers
in the same occupation in the same area. 20 C.F.R. § 655.10. The prevailing wage, alone, is insufficient
to establish whether a salary is high in relation to others in the field, as required by the plain language
of the regulation. The salary screenshot mentioned above only provided average and median salary
data for market research analysts and marketing specialists and did not identify the high-end salaries
for those performing work with similar responsibilities as the Beneficiary. Therefore, the Petitioner
has not shown the proposed salary on the Form I-129 constitutes a high salary consistent with the plain
language of the regulation.
Further, while the regulatory language of the criterion also allows for evidence of "other remuneration
for services," the Petitioner did not provide evidence showing these other incentives, and that they are
high in relation to others in the field. Finally, as mentioned by the Director, according to the Petitioner's
signed employment agreement dated May 8, 2017, the Beneficiary will be paid $42,000 per year, and
other compensation. The inconsistency between the wage stated on Form I-129, and that in the
employment agreement prevents us from determining the Beneficiary's salary and whether it is
considered high in relation to others in the field.
Based on the foregoing, the Petitioner has not established that the Beneficiary satisfies the criterion at
8 C.F.R. § 214.2(o)(3)(iii)(B)(8).
